pf.license.need: Usually none for a sitter in a family's home. A play room where parents leave children (drop-in child care) needs a child-care license where the state's rules require it. The state form says which.
pf.license.ask: Babysitting and tutoring: the company's business registration, where the form asks for one. A play room: its child-care license number, where the state's rules require one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Sitters hold no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.background_checks: A switch, per business and per state. Where the state's rules require one, a sitter isn't offered until it's on file. Each sitter's check shows only as run or seen: who ran it, what it searched, and the date. Never 'vetted' or 'safe'.
pf.license.agency_rules: Where the state's rules license a sitter or nanny agency, or an employment agency that places nannies, the form asks for it here.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Insured or bonded is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.not_this_work: Placing a nanny the family hires as its own employee is not booked through Rosie.

what_happens: A child hurt, missing, alone, not breathing or choking, or a serious reaction: 'Call 911 now.' No booking in that chat.
A report of harm to a child: 911 first if a child is in danger now. Then a person on Rosie's team takes the report and follows the reporting steps the state's rules set. No booking in that chat.
A sick child: Rosie gives no medical advice. Health details go on the secure page, and the owner decides if a sitter can come.
Medicine questions: medicine is given only with the parent's written instructions on the secure page, never on a text.

pf.first_steps.family_page: The family page on the secure page, before the first sitting: children, allergies, medicines with written instructions, bedtimes, house rules, who may collect, the emergency contact. At the play room it's the form signed while booking.
pf.first_steps.school_pick_up: For a school pick-up, the parent adds the sitter to the school's own pick-up list first.

pf.visit.check_in: At home: the parent gives the code at the door, the sitter texts it in, and the parent shows the house before leaving. At the play room: the code at the front desk, and the child is ticked on the session's roster.
pf.visit.hand_back: The children are handed back only to the parent or an adult on the family page's pick-up list, after a photo ID check if the sitter doesn't know them. Anyone else waits while the parent is asked.
pf.visit.never_alone: A sitter never leaves the children alone. If the parent is late, the sitter stays, the extra time is billed at the agreed rate, and the owner is told.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Extra time only at the agreed rate, after the sitter says yes. Nothing else is added at the visit.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with the real end time once a parent is home. The play room's sign-out is the same code at the desk.
pf.visit.pick_up_changes: A text naming someone new is only the parent's request: the parent adds them on the family page, and the sitter checks photo ID.

pf.money.start: At home: a card saved at booking, nothing charged. After the sitting, the bill is texted (the parent replies 1 or pays on the page, with a tip), or the card is charged at DONE. Play room: a card saved for the fee and paid at the desk, or paid in full for a camp day.
pf.money.hourly: The hours are counted from the start to the real end, with the minimum. Extra time is in 15-minute blocks, only if the sitter agreed to stay.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel (within 24 hours) or nobody home: the business's own fee (the example: $72, 3 hours), never more than the booking. The play room's no-show or late-cancel fee: $20. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.plans: Each plan visit is charged after it's done. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: Optional, on the pay page, all to the sitter, where the owner turns the tip line on.
pf.money.tax: A tax line only where the state's rules tax this work, from the state form.

pf.messages.photos: Photos of children are never shown, and the photo question isn't asked.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish. The sitter's languages show on the booking.
pf.messages.minors: Texts go only to the parent's phone, never to a child.

skills: CPR and first aid (the card's date shows)

pf.staff.checks: Each sitter's ID and age check, and any background check, show only as run or seen, with the date. A sitter under 18 is never listed unless the owner and the state's rules allow it.
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so. A play room follows the state's staff ratio and checks, from the state form.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A stand-in sitter is offered to the family first, with that sitter's own checks, and never sent without the family's OK. No answer: the owner calls.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs new families, overnights and driving. The office manager may answer booking requests; the owner's answer wins. Fees are the owner's alone.

pf.rules.never_alone: A sitter never leaves a child alone, whatever the time.
pf.rules.pick_up: A child goes home only with an adult on the family page's list, after a photo ID check.
pf.rules.medicine: Medicine only with the parent's written instructions on the secure page.
plans: The plan's terms show before any card: the days, the hours, the price a visit, when it's charged, and how to skip, pause or end.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
pf.rules.reporting: Where the state's rules require a report of suspected harm to a child, the business and Rosie's team follow them.
pf.rules.nanny_hiring: Placing a nanny the family employs is not booked through Rosie. Where the state's rules license an agency that places nannies, that is the agency's own business.
pf.rules.play_room: Ratios, sign-in and sign-out records, and any immunization records follow the state's child-care rules, from the state form.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, except the health note, which is deleted after the job.

matter_most: A parent home late: the sitter is asked to stay, at $6 for each 15 minutes. If the sitter can't stay, the sitter still never leaves the children alone, and the owner is told.
Someone not on the pick-up list comes for a child: no child leaves; the parent is texted at once.
A pick-up change sent by text: the parent adds the person on the family page first.
A child is hurt or has a reaction: 911 first, then the parent; no health detail in any text.
The sitter can't come: a stand-in with their own checks is offered first, never assumed.
Late cancel or nobody home: the owner decides the fee.
A parent questions the hours on the bill: the owner checks with the sitter and sends the corrected total.
A new family: the owner's OK and a meet-and-greet first.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
From: cleaner. A sitter works like a home cleaner: a visit at the family's home, the same person each time, a stand-in only with the family's yes, an after-school plan, a card saved and charged after. Flow A borrows the yoga pilot's seat-in-a-session shape, with a child handed back only to an approved adult (A8-42), the way the brief says daycare and camps run.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Family Sitters sends a sitter to the family's home (babysitting, plus tutoring as its second kind of work). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Kids' Club, Sam's second company, a play room where parents book a drop-in spot and collect the child after. The old flowchart has only the at-home side, so flow A is built from the plug-in.
Names: the sitters are Taylor and Devon; the play room leads are Toni and Shay. Alex's partner is Chris (the pilot's Jamie is a cleaner word), and the grandmother is Grace. All neutral, so every he, she or they in the master still fits. Addresses: 15 Aspen Ct (the family), 410 Grove St (the office), 26 Linden St (the play room).
Prices are the example agency's own, not a standard: $24 an hour for 1 or 2 children with a 3-hour minimum, +$3 an hour for each extra child, $30 an hour after midnight, $180 overnight (Sam OKs it), $6 for each 15 minutes a parent is late, a $72 after-school plan visit, $35 tutoring an hour. Play room: $35 drop-in, $55 play camp, $20 fee. The main sitting is 4½ hours: $108.
Money paths, from the old flowchart: a card is saved at booking and nothing is taken; the bill is texted when the sitter texts DONE (reply 1, or pay on the page with a tip), or the card is charged at DONE. Sitting never takes a hold, a deposit or the full price. So B lists list|card|bill (main) and list|card|card.
Flow A lists list|card|counter (main: a card saved for the $20 fee, paid at the desk at pick-up) and list|full|none (a play camp day, paid in full when booking). The club never holds money.
Sign-up words (S1-12 to S1-17, S1-21, S1-41 to S1-47, S1-57) are rewritten to how sitting is paid: cards only, nothing taken before, the bill or the card after. The master's barbershop and plumbing examples became the play room and sitting.
Late cancel (after 6pm the day before) or nobody home: the $72 fee, only if Sam confirms it; no answer, no fee. This is the old flowchart's own rule and amount.
Children's details are private. Names, ages, allergies, medicines, bedtimes, the emergency contact and who may collect them go only on the family page (B4-34, A4-72), seen only by the booked sitter or lead. No text ever names a child's health, and medicine questions are pointed to the page (B7-16).
A new family gets a free 20-minute meet-and-greet first (the master's first step, B4-38 and B4-40), and Sam OKs every new family (B6-03 'Sam's OK first'). Both are on the main path, since the old flowchart had the owner accept a new family.
